T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 6/6 frozen cases: original-result replay, changed-body rejection, foreign replay denial, tax-change stability and concurrent identical/mismatched keys all pass under a customer-level boundary.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases stop at GET quote missing points, an explicitly disclosed gap; supplemental four yielding scenarios conserve applied points and ledger balances.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures pass with pricing before writes; supplemental second saveLot fault leaves balances [0,123,500] and no rollback, matching the report caveat.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: pricing/domain/quote.ts caps pointsCents after discount and rounds tax on the reduced nonnegative base.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: pure allocatePoints filters strict expiry at supplied now, sorts earliest-first and captures partial allocation provenance.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 6/6: ownedOrder precedes replay; stored original quote/request values, debit and saveRedemption are covered by the same customer KeyedLock.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: KeyedLock covers full debit/publication and compatible cancellation with reliable finally release, and supplemental yielding races conserve points; second saveLot failure strands the first debit without compensation.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: splitRestorable uses original expiry, restores exact source IDs and reversed flag/pending cancellation prevent repeat refunds under the same lock.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental changed-owner replay 404: ownedOrder is checked before replay and before refund; withCustomer returns 401 for missing session.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: assertPending is inside the same customer lock used by cancel and before any allocation writes.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next lotsFor reads all customer history: 10 -> 3010 records (budget 36), six calls; only changed lots are written and replay one call/two records, but no usable-lot index/filter.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Thin routes only validate/map outcomes; application/order-payments.ts coordinates ownership, locking and stores; pure own-domain pricing/allocation/reversal planners take explicit time, wired through createApp.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms 24/24 with 15 new tests; report expressly discloses pre-points GET quotes, absent typecheck, uncompensated debit/refund failures and process-local serialization.
